- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days) by forecasting further gains; cap or dampen subsequent peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show upward trend, model often continues upward; if sentiment turns neutral or negative, reduce forecast slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5-7 days) — apply downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.3 → +0.2), model often misses the reversal; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment momentum shift.
- When sentiment is flat or low (≤ 0.2), model often overestimates — apply downward correction to avoid “false optimism” bias.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >3% for 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1-2% per day to reflect diminishing momentum or market correction.
